events.title: Battle of Trenton
events.description: George Washington's Continental Army, having crossed the icy Delaware River the previous night, launched a surprise attack on Hessian forces garrisoned at Trenton, New Jersey, capturing roughly 900 soldiers with very few American casualties.
events.significance: The victory revived American morale and enlistments after a string of defeats in 1776, and it helped keep the Revolutionary War effort alive at a critical moment.

events.title: Marie and Pierre Curie Announce the Discovery of Radium
events.description: Marie and Pierre Curie, working with Gustave Bémont, announced to the French Academy of Sciences the discovery of a new radioactive element, which they named radium, isolated from pitchblende.
events.significance: The discovery advanced the understanding of radioactivity, opened the way to radiation therapy for cancer, and contributed to the development of modern nuclear physics.

events.title: Dissolution of the Soviet Union
events.description: The Soviet of the Republics, the upper chamber of the Supreme Soviet, formally voted the Soviet Union out of existence, a day after Mikhail Gorbachev resigned as president.
events.significance: It marked the formal end of the USSR and the Cold War, and it led to the emergence of fifteen independent nations and a reshaped global order.

events.title: Indian Ocean Earthquake and Tsunami
events.description: A magnitude 9.1 undersea earthquake off the coast of Sumatra, Indonesia, generated massive tsunamis that struck coastlines across the Indian Ocean, killing an estimated 230,000 people in 14 countries.
events.significance: It was one of the deadliest natural disasters in recorded history and led to major advances in international tsunami warning systems and disaster response coordination.

events.title: Death of Harry S. Truman
events.description: Harry S. Truman, the 33rd President of the United States, died in Kansas City, Missouri, at age 88. He had led the nation through the end of World War II, the decision to use atomic bombs on Japan, and the start of the Cold War.
events.significance: Truman's presidency shaped the postwar world through the Marshall Plan, NATO, the Truman Doctrine, and the Korean War response.
